history_vintages.why: 'The Company is a global manufacturer and marketer of semiconductor devices, principally DRAM and NAND Flash memory and CMOS image sensors.' 'We have experienced dramatic declines in average selling prices for our semiconductor memory products which have adversely affected our business.' 'The semiconductor memory industry is highly competitive.' 'Some of our competitors are large corporations or conglomerates that may have greater resources to withstand downturns in the semiconductor markets in which we compete' (FY2007 10-K); DURABLE: no Micron 10-K calls its own business cyclical (CYCLICAL needs the company's 'our business is cyclical', as BKR, CAT and NVDA said; the F and AVGO reading of industry words), so the kind is DURABLE, the label only; no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a memory maker (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so the watch list is empty

eps_excluded.2006: a year distorted by one-off benefits (the AVGO FY2018 mirror test): its $408M net income ($0.57 a diluted share) includes '$230 million of net proceeds for the sale of the Company’s existing NAND Flash memory designs ... to Intel' and '$23 million in additional amounts expected to be reimbursed resulting from the extension of an economic development agreement' (FY2007 10-K): $253M of listed benefits against $155M of income without them, so reported EPS is 2.7 times the $0.21 without them (the $230M alone against $178M; with the year's whole $18M tax provision charged to it, $212M against $196M); no figure excluding them was published, so no P/E. FY2007 is a loss, so starting the history after FY2006 would leave no year: only the year itself leaves (the NKE FY2018 reading of 'would leave neither')

revenue.measure: revenue growth, % (five-year selected data of the latest 10-K reporting both years)

rows: Research and development ("R&D") expenses vary primarily with the number of development wafers processed, the cost of advanced equipment dedicated to new product and process development, and personnel costs. The Company deems development of a product complete once the product has been thoroughly reviewed and tested for performance and reliability and is internally qualified for sale to customers. Because of the lead times necessary to manufacture the Company's products, the Company typically begins to process a significant volume of product before it is internally qualified. As a result, R&D expenses can vary significantly depending on the timing of product qualification. Product development costs are recorded as R&D expense. The Company's R&D expenses were $656.4 million, $561.3 million and $489.5 million in 2003, 2002 and 2001, respectively.

opex_gap.measure: growth of R&D plus SG&A less net sales growth, pp (statements of operations, three years)

inventory_gap.measure: year-end inventory growth less net sales growth, pp (each year's own 10-K)

fiscal_calendar.quote: The Company operates on a 52/53 week fiscal year which ends on the Thursday closest to August 31.

fy2003_end.quote: Fiscal years 2003, 2002 and 2001 each contained 52 weeks and ended on August 28, 2003, August 29, 2002, and August 30, 2001, respectively.

price_basis: Yahoo's MU series is adjusted for the splits of 1994-04-19, 1995-05-23 and 2000-05-02; none is later than the P/E window's start (2003-08-29), so every price the models use is the close as traded.
